title: 1931 Ford Model AA Display Carrier
subtitle: Vintage Heavy Hauler & Cage-Car Transport Rig
summary: A vintage 1931 Ford Model AA truck re-engineered as an open-chassis display carrier, built to haul and exhibit open-cage race cars and custom chassis builds.
narrative: Inspired by conversations with custom shop builder Omar regarding dedicated display rigs for open-cage tube-frame cars.

This study pairs a heavy-duty 1931 Ford Model AA commercial cab and chassis with custom ramp geometry, transforming a classic pre-war workhorse into an eye-catching platform designed to showcase raw space-frame craftsmanship at events and shop displays.

title: Sakura Soda Pop: Mk1 Capri
subtitle: 700+ WHP EA888 2.0L Compound-Turbo AWD Beast
summary: Because 2.0L is a drink size, not an engine! A Mk1 Ford Capri engineered around a boosted VW/Audi EA888 2.0L with compound turbos, DSG transmission, and 4MOTION AWD.

specifications.engine: 2.0L VW/Audi EA888 Inline-4 w/ Staged Compound Turbos (700+ WHP)
specifications.drivetrain: 4MOTION All-Wheel Drive w/ Widened MQB Suspension

narrative: Soda Pop plays on the classic gearhead jab that '2.0L is a drink size, not an engine!' by dropping a high-boost 2.0L EA888 engine into a featherweight Mk1 Ford Capri.
Mated to a tuned DSG transmission and 4MOTION AWD drivetrain over widened MQB geometry, custom box flares house 295-width Hoosier R-compound tires on center-lock wheels.
Featured here blowing past a carbon-bodied supercar along Route 66 near Cadillac Ranch for the Mother Road Centennial (1926–2026) in both classic Aqua Marine and the custom Sakura blossom livery.

title: Project Lynx: Mid-Engine AWD Concept
subtitle: Mid-Engine e-AWD & Active Aero Performance Study
summary: A mid-engine, all-wheel-drive sports car design fantasy combining classic wedge supercar proportions with active aerodynamics and e-AWD torque vectoring.
narrative: Project Lynx explores an aggressive mid-engine AWD platform configured for high-speed stability and extreme cornering dynamics.
Blending iconic 1970s Italian-American wedge styling with active aerodynamic vacuum blowers and e-AWD front electric motors, Lynx delivers pure high-concept vision.

title: 1954 Willys Aero AWD Concept
subtitle: All-Wheel Drive Compact Performance Study
summary: An all-wheel-drive performance conversion concept bringing modern traction and turbocharged muscle to the classic 1954 Willys Aero compact body.
narrative: The 1954 Willys Aero combined lightweight unibody efficiency with streamlined post-war design.
This fantasy conversion pairs the Aero shell with a modern high-output engine and advanced AWD transfer case, turning the innocent 1950s commuter into an all-weather sleeper missile.

title: Mid-Engine 'Cuda Concept
subtitle: Transverse Mid-Ship Mopar Performance Study
summary: A radical mid-engine layout exploration taking the aggressive proportions of the Plymouth Barracuda and re-centering the V8 powerplant behind the driver.
narrative: Re-imagining the iconic E-Body muscle car architecture through the lens of supercar dynamics.
By placing the engine mid-ship, weight distribution achieves optimal rear bias while maintaining the wide-track, menacing nose profile of the legendary Barracuda.

title: 1951 Hudson Pacemaker Custom
subtitle: Step-Down Chassis Lowrider & Cruiser Concept
summary: A tailored design study celebrating Hudson's famous step-down floorpan architecture with lowered air stance and shaved custom trim.
narrative: Hudson's revolutionary Step-Down chassis dropped the passenger floorpan inside the frame rails, giving the 1951 Pacemaker a naturally low center of gravity and low roofline long before it was standard.
This fantasy study accentuates those swept lines with bagged air suspension, seamless bodywork, and custom rolling stock.

title: Il Lungo: Stretched Fiat Paint Experiment
subtitle: Extended Silhouette & Experimental Finish Study
summary: A creative styling exploration extending a classic Fiat body shell into a sleek proportion while experimenting with depth-rich paint and clearcoat techniques.
narrative: Il Lungo (The Long One) plays with proportion and light refraction, stretching the European compact silhouette into an elongated street cruiser.
The primary focus of this study is testing rich, multi-layer candy depth and custom clearcoat formulations against dramatic body curves.

title: Van Nuys Blvd Cruisin' Situation
subtitle: Omar's Firebird & '63 Caddy Imagined Back in the Day
summary: A nostalgic period scene placing Omar's custom Firebird alongside a classic '63 Cadillac cruising Van Nuys Boulevard during the golden era of SoCal street culture.
narrative: Rather than a single vehicle build concept, this is a fantasy situation—a period-authentic homage to Wednesday night cruising on Van Nuys Boulevard.

Captured under the boulevard neon lights, Double-O Garage owner Omar's Firebird rolls alongside a low-slung '63 Cadillac, recreating the peak era of South Bay and San Fernando Valley cruising history.

title: Night Wraith: '65 Cadillac Convertible
subtitle: Slammed Air Ride & Twin-Boosted Cruiser
summary: A radical 1965 Cadillac Convertible restomod concept engineered with ultra-low air ride suspension, custom narrow rear suicide doors, a high-output LS V8, and subtle ghosted graphics.
narrative: Night Wraith explores taking the commanding length and iconic tailfins of the 1965 Cadillac Convertible and dropping it flat against the pavement with modern air suspension geometry.

The custom bodywork features re-engineered narrow rear suicide doors for seamless passenger ingress, shaved brightwork, ghosted graphics, and a twin-boosted LS V8 delivering modern reliability and effortless street presence.

gallery.caption: Night Wraith — Primary stance profile showcasing lowered air ride geometry and custom body lines.
Night Wraith — Ride height and suspension travel comparison study.

title: 1950 Plymouth Suburban Station Wagon
subtitle: Early All-Steel Wagon Lowrider & Custom Concept
summary: An exploratory design concept reviving Plymouth's iconic 1950 all-steel 2-door wagon with slammed stance, custom brightwork, and modern proportions.
narrative: The 1950 Plymouth Suburban was a pioneer in American automotive history as one of the first all-steel station wagons brought to market.

This fantasy concept reimagines the classic 2-door wagon silhouette with modern air suspension geometry, smoothed body contours, and a street-cruiser stance while honoring its vintage chrome grille and fastback roofline.

title: 1969 Chevrolet Suburban Custom Hauler
subtitle: 3-Door Action Line Pro-Touring & Stance Study
summary: A high-concept styling study on the legendary 1969 Action Line 3-door Suburban, featuring tucked big wheels, clean bodywork, and modern muscle attitude.
narrative: Built on the unique 1967-1972 C10/C20 Action Line 3-door body style (one door on the driver side, two on the passenger side), the 1969 Suburban remains an iconic utility canvas.
This study examines slamming the heavy-duty hauler over oversized forged wheels, shaving trim for ultra-clean flanks, and delivering pure street-hauler presence.

title: Wicked J GTR Concept
subtitle: 1951 Henry J TDI Transverse Track Weapon
summary: A radical track-focused restomod concept dropping a high-output 1.9L TDI turbodiesel and 02M 6-speed transmission into a flared 1951 Henry J shell.

specifications.chassis: Custom Tube Space Frame w/ Track Geometry

narrative: The Wicked J GTR explores taking one of America's original economy compacts—the 1951 Henry J—and transforming it into an ultra-agile, high-torque track beast.

Underneath the aggressively widened fenders sits a tuned 1.9L TDI turbodiesel engine backed by a VW 02M 6-speed manual transmission, offering extreme low-end torque and bulletproof gearing in a featherweight chassis.
Featured here in two distinct visual directions: an iconic classic racing-striped livery and a high-visibility Toxic track specification.

gallery.caption: Wicked J GTR — Heritage Motorsport Livery with dual center stripes and aggressively radiused wheel arches.
Wicked J GTR — Toxic Green Track Spec showcasing maximum aero stance and wide-bore side exhaust setup.

title: 1939 Ford COE Carnivore RV Restomod
subtitle: Supercharged 5.2L Long-Haul Overland Hauler
summary: A 1939 Ford Cab-Over-Engine RV restomod powered by a supercharged 5.2L Carnivore V8 (720 hp / 640 lb-ft) and 10R140 10-speed transmission, engineered specifically for high-speed desert blasts and steep mountain passes.

specifications.chassis: Custom Boxed Chassis w/ IFS & Coilovers

narrative: Forged from the bones of a 1939 Ford COE, the heart of this restomod is Ford's supercharged 5.2-liter Carnivore V8 delivering 640 lb-ft of torque and 720 horsepower managed by Ford's heavy-duty 10R140 TorqShift 10-speed automatic transmission, delivering lightning-fast gear changes and relentless acceleration without missing a beat under load.

Riding on a custom boxed chassis fitted with independent front suspension and adjustable coil-over shocks, the rig is built for effortless highway cruising and confident mountain ascents. It is spec'd directly for purpose-driven long-haul runs out of Los Angeles: effortlessly holding pace during high-speed desert blasts to Las Vegas, tackling the steep grade and sub-zero conditions on ski trips up to Mammoth, or carving through the sweepers along Highway 395 and the Pacific Coast Highway. Engineering precision meets raw, unstoppable capability.

title: The Talladega Transaxle: '69 Mid-Engine Concept
subtitle: The Cancelled '69 Supercar Study
summary: A radical, mid-engine concept fusing Ford's low-drag 1969 Torino Talladega aero nose with a mid-mounted 427 Cammer SOHC V8 and GT40 Hewland transaxle.
narrative: HISTORICAL DISCLAIMER: This vehicle concept, narrative, and historical background are entirely fictional. Project 69-M is an alternate-history design study exploring a what if crossover between Ford's NASCAR aero program and Le Mans mid-engine architecture.

This single prototype is all that remains of Project 69-M, Ford's radical, black-budget attempt to rewrite the rules of both NASCAR and the street. The concept was a direct fusion: take the low-drag, extended nose and flush grille of the homologation-bound 1969 Torino Talladega and mount it on a mid-engine chassis.

While the race cars would always be front-engine (NASCAR rules demanded it), Ford planned to sell 500 mid-engine T-Transaxles as a production vehicle, creating an exotic aero-king to beat Ferrari on the street and Dodge on the high banks. The large mid-body intakes, seen on the production C8 Corvette-like profile, were designed to feed a planned massive mid-ship powertrain.

To explain its mid-engine architecture, Ford engineers created the ultimate what if setup: They took a race-ready 7.0-liter (427 cu in) Ford Cammer SOHC V8, but instead of mounting it in the front, they reversed it, mounting it directly behind the driver. The original Ford Toploader transmission was scrapped. Instead, the Cammer was mated to a custom-cast, heavy-duty Hewland LG transaxle—the same reliable box used in Ford's GT40 program.

This '69 prototype, thus, was not just a styling exercise; it was an authentic integration of Ford's two greatest performance eras, pairing the high-drag oval-track nose with the mid-ship transaxle of Le Mans. The modern, 5-spoke alloys and updated side intakes were added decades later during a modern sympathetic restoration, preparing it for a single, high-speed test run on the gravel road of the skunkworks' private facility.

title: GMC Crackerbox Series (1959-1968)
subtitle: Forward Control Heavy Hauler Explorations
summary: Custom forward-control studies based on the legendary 1959-1968 GMC D/DB Series Crackerbox cab, spanning extreme 6x6 builds, flatbed car haulers, and desert off-road transport rigs.
narrative: A focused design exploration into GMC's iconic 1959-1968 D/DB Series forward-control commercial cab, affectionately known as the Crackerbox.
This series examines the extreme versatility of the ultra-short cab architecture across high-capability off-road transport, vintage car hauling, and heavy-duty mechanical conversions.

subtitle: Extreme Off-Road Performance Fusion
summary: A mid-engine, trophy-truck-based concept merging a Camaro body shell with extreme off-road capability.
